title: Post-Intubation Management
keywords: post-intubation hypotension reduce PEEP exclude tension PTX treat hypovolaemia mainstem
sources: Critical Vector — EM Pocket Guide: Post-Intubation Management

changelog.change: Initial entry — initial vent settings, confirm/secure/stabilise checklist, analgosedation, and the post-intubation hypotension differential.

summary: The five minutes after the tube goes in kill people. Set lung-protective ventilation, confirm placement with waveform capnography and a film, start analgesia-first sedation, and immediately work the post-intubation hypotension differential (PEEP, tension pneumothorax, hypovolaemia, mainstem, the induction agent).

rows: 6–8 mL/kg ideal body weight (6 if ARDS or at risk)
12–16/min; adjust to pH ≥ 7.35 (match a high pre-intubation minute ventilation in metabolic acidosis or asthma)
5 cmH₂O (up the ARDSNet ladder if ARDS)
1:2 (1:3–1:4 for asthma/COPD to avoid air trapping)

items: Waveform capnography — the gold standard; a flat capnogram = oesophageal (or arrest).
Bilateral breath sounds, no epigastric gurgling.
Portable chest X-ray: tube tip 3–5 cm above the carina.
Secure the tube; document the cm marking at the lips/teeth.

Analgesia-first sedation: a fentanyl infusion + propofol 5–50 mcg/kg/min OR dexmedetomidine 0.2–1.5 mcg/kg/h. Target a light level (RASS 0 to −2) unless deep sedation is indicated. Do NOT leave a paralysed patient under-sedated.

body.text: Post-intubation hypotension — work it fast: (1) high PEEP / breath stacking → reduce PEEP, disconnect and let an obstructive patient exhale; (2) tension pneumothorax → decompress; (3) hypovolaemia unmasked by the loss of sympathetic drive and positive pressure → fluid bolus, push-dose vasopressor; (4) right mainstem intubation → pull the tube back; (5) the induction agent (propofol) → support and switch. Also give analgesia and check a glucose/K+ if the arrest risk is rising.
